stem: A low-risk administrative task and a time-sensitive quarantine identity issue are both unfinished. Which should normally be prioritized?
choices: Finish the low-risk administrative task first because quick closure reduces the open-task count.
Use a neutral ordering rule such as first-in/first-out so personal judgment does not bias priority.
Treat both items as equal until a supervisor explicitly assigns priority.
Prioritize the quarantine/identity issue because its consequence, time sensitivity, and downstream dependency are materially greater.
rationale: Priority should reflect consequence, urgency, and dependency—not ease or arbitrary ordering. A quarantine/identity issue can affect containment, traceability, release, and multiple downstream tasks, so it normally outranks a low-risk administrative item. The handoff should make that reasoning explicit so the next shift understands why the issue is first.
